density_challenge: The opposite case is that this unit is supplement-grade, not standalone, for a series about the book Palantir sent. Verification found the quotes mostly clean, but nearly all of them come from Allen's later talks, handouts and website copy (2008-2020). The only first-hand book text is 3,647 words of the 2001 edition, ending in chapter 1. Nothing from the Five Stages chapter, the processing chapter, the weekly review chapter or the 2015 edition body was read, and the excerpt contains no two-minute rule, so a script must say 'Allen says' and never 'the book says'. The two-version angle is likewise impossible, and the edition Palantir sent is unknown. Qureshi's single sentence names the book without an edition, and Lonsdale's clause sits on a page with no byline whose intro is third person, so the Palantir link is thin and the unit cannot say why the book was handed to new hires. The mechanisms rest on assertions Allen presents without sources (four-item limit, no sense of past or future, false sense of control, 90+% of lists incomplete, 30-40% of emails), and the proposed demonstrations (interruption counters falling to zero) would show an effect nobody has measured. The numbers also disagree: 30-100 versus 70-100 projects, and 150-220 versus 150-200 versus 120 next actions. Two attributions needed repair, and some of the sources are live pages that were edited after their stated dates (the what-is-gtd page in 2024, a 2010 post in 2018), so exact wording may drift. The case for 'standalone' still holds if the video is framed as 'Allen's method as he describes it', since all of that checks out against author-owned sources and nine minutes is feasible. Fixes: change two 2001 locators from Introduction to chapter 1, drop '同时' from about-2015-edition, and reattribute the naming essay to the company site. Locator note: the explorer's scratch line numbers differ from a fresh strip by about 3 lines in the Ferriss text, so locate by paragraph. Everything else I confirmed by direct re-read.
